_comment: Fragment 63 — the remaining B-019..B-031 entries anchored to their own files. Merged 2026-08-24.

nodes.label: B-019 — A Rule That Stopped the Lane It Had Authorised
nodes.description: The build lane was selected for a turn and read the governing rule as requiring a further boundary act before it could begin, so it did not begin.
nodes.rationale: The two statements could not both hold, and the lane behaved correctly against the one it could read. Recorded so no later lane needs conversation context to resolve it.

nodes.label: B-020 — Config Coupling Proves Names, Not the Required Values
nodes.description: A green coupling result was being treated as a complete configuration oracle for the sprint, when it establishes only that an identifier appears on both sides.
nodes.rationale: A declaration contradicting its own published value passes the check, so the completeness claim has to rest on the unit tests instead.

nodes.label: B-021 — The Fixture Runner Guards a Dirty Start, Not a Concurrent Reader
nodes.description: The runner refuses to begin on a dirty tree and restores what it mutates, but nothing protects it from another process touching the same files while it runs.
nodes.rationale: It was proven on the turn that answered it: a concurrent stash defeated a restore and a required template field was deleted.

nodes.label: B-022 — The Readiness-Review Turn Report
nodes.description: The build lane reported what it reviewed before accepting work, separating what it completed from what it found open.
nodes.rationale: The first report the channel received under the rule that a turn ends with one, written because an empty report and a lane that never ran are otherwise indistinguishable.

nodes.label: B-023 — Separate the Repository Lock From Work Readiness
nodes.description: A proposal to describe the repository lock and the state of the work as two independent axes rather than one set of four terms.
nodes.rationale: Adopted in substance and rejected in form: the conflation was real and the second vocabulary was not taken, because the work condition already lives in the entries and the turn report.

nodes.label: B-025 — The Reopens-Phase Check Had No Tracked Negative Proof
nodes.description: An entry claimed the reopening control had been negative-tested three ways, and no fixture for it existed in the repository.
nodes.rationale: Reopening presupposes a closure and no phase has ever closed, which is exactly the property that makes the control non-vacuous and exactly what had never been demonstrated.

nodes.label: B-026 — The Selected-Turn Report for the Configuration Sprint
nodes.description: The build lane recorded what it completed, what it specified without applying, and what remained open, including that no commit had been created because the index and working tree described different deliverables.
nodes.rationale: It requested a two-boundary return sequence. The Chief Editor instead directed the orchestration lane to take over, so the work is kept and committed by the other lane as a declared crossing.

nodes.label: B-027 — The Entry Template Restated Live Lane State
nodes.description: A dated claim about which lane held the lock was appended to the reusable entry template, so every copy carried a status that had already moved.
nodes.rationale: The same drift mechanism the rule files had already had this removed from, missed in one file.

nodes.label: B-030 — Committing the Index Would Have Published a Stale Packet
nodes.description: The index held pre-clarification versions of several entries while the implementation they reported sat unstaged and untracked.
nodes.rationale: A valid commit identifier would have been attached to the wrong bytes, and a later commit can repair files but cannot make the first evidence claim true.

nodes.label: B-031 — The Takeover and Completion Guide
nodes.description: An executable sequence turning the lane rules into two turns: finish and commit the configuration sprint, return control, then complete the later stages once the schema decisions are final.
nodes.rationale: Its routing was superseded by the Chief Editor directing a takeover, but its staging, verification and graph-synchronisation procedure was adopted and executed, and its second-takeover plan remains the live route to the later stages.
